# HIIT Rowing Workout: 5 Interval Sessions From 10 to 30 Minutes (Beginner to Advanced)


Last updated November 2026


Two minutes on the interval clock, and a leaderboard full of people to catch.


**Short answer:** A HIIT rowing workout alternates short, hard efforts with easy rowing to recover. Work intervals last 20 seconds to 4 minutes at about 8 or 9 out of 10 effort, and a full session takes 10 to 30 minutes, warm-up included. New to it? Start with 20 seconds hard and 40 seconds easy, six times. Two or three sessions a week is plenty. The five workouts below run from that 10-minute starter to a 30-minute 4x4.


A rower is a great machine for intervals. Every stroke works your legs, glutes, back, arms and core, nothing pounds your joints, and you can go from easy to all-out within a few strokes.


Paul Kerling's family also owns a Peloton bike and FightCamp. Here's how he sums up the rower:


"I exert more energy on this rower in the same amount of time than any other piece of fitness equipment."

## What Is a HIIT Rowing Workout?


HIIT (high-intensity interval training) means short bursts of hard work with easy recovery in between. On a rower, "hard" means driving harder with your legs while keeping the stroke under control. "Easy" means light pressure at a relaxed pace. You never fully stop, so your heart rate stays up and your technique stays smooth.


The appeal is how little time it takes. In a[2016 McMaster University study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4846072/) , sedentary men did three 10-minute sessions a week, each with just one minute of all-out effort. After 12 weeks their peak oxygen uptake had risen 19%, the same gain as a group that cycled steadily for 45 minutes per session. That study used bikes and small groups, but the idea applies to any machine you can push hard. The[World Health Organization's guidelines](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7719906/) make a similar trade: 75 minutes of vigorous activity a week counts the same as 150 minutes of moderate activity.


Every stroke uses your legs, glutes, back, arms and core, which is why 20 hard seconds on a rower feels like a lot more.


## How Hard Should HIIT Rowing Feel?


Use a 1 to 10 effort scale, where 10 is the hardest you can go, and back it up with the talk test. Stroke rate (strokes per minute, or spm, on your monitor) is only a rough guide:


Effort Out of 10 Talk test Stroke rate (rough guide)


Easy (recovery) 3 to 4 Full sentences 18 to 22 spm


Hard 7 to 8 A few words at a time 24 to 28 spm


Max 9 to 10 No talking 28 to 32 spm or more


The most common mistake is trying to go harder by rowing faster. A higher stroke rate with the same leg drive just gives you more short, choppy strokes. Push harder through the foot plates first, and let the rate climb a little on its own.


A heart rate monitor takes out the guesswork, especially in the easy blocks. If your heart rate never comes down between intervals, you're recovering too hard.

## 1. What's a Good 10-Minute HIIT Rowing Workout for Beginners?


Beginner · 10 minutes


1. **Warm up:** 2 minutes easy
2. **Intervals:** 6 rounds of 20 seconds hard (7 to 8 out of 10), then 40 seconds easy
3. **Cool down:** 2 minutes easy


Twenty seconds is short enough to hold good form all the way through, and 40 seconds is long enough to actually recover. When all six rounds feel manageable, move to 30 seconds hard and 30 easy. On the Strong Series, Short Stack (6 to 9 minutes of short intervals with rising resistance) is the ready-made version.


One warning about "just 10 minutes," from Strong Series owner Greg LaCour:


"I always think I am only going to work out for 10 minutes but it has consistently turned into 30 or 40 minutes."


**Greg LaCour** , Strong Series Rower owner · Verified Buyer


## 2. How Do You Do a Rowing Pyramid? (15 Minutes)


Beginner to intermediate · 15 minutes


1. **Warm up:** 5 minutes easy, with three 10-stroke pushes in the last 2 minutes
2. **Pyramid:** 30 seconds hard, 30 easy; 45 hard, 45 easy; 60 hard, 60 easy; 45 hard, 45 easy; 30 hard, 30 easy
3. **Cool down:** 3 minutes easy


Pyramids teach pacing. Go out too hot in the first 30 seconds and the 60-second middle will let you know. Aim to hold the same split (your pace per 500 meters) on every hard piece. On the Strong Series, Power Pyramid (10 to 14 minutes) builds stroke-rate control the same way, and coach John's Twenty's Plenty classes work through pyramids, ladders and waves.


## 3. What's the Best 20-Minute HIIT Rowing Workout?


Intermediate · 20 minutes


1. **Warm up:** 5 minutes easy
2. **Intervals:** 10 rounds of 40 seconds hard (8 out of 10), then 20 seconds easy
3. **Cool down:** 5 minutes easy


That's 6 minutes and 40 seconds of hard work packed into 10, and those 20-second breaks start to feel very short by round six.[Concept2 calls 40/20](https://www.concept2.com/blog/the-best-rowing-machine-workouts) its best workout for when you only have 20 minutes. On the Strong Series, HIIT Highway (9 to 25 minutes of fast 30-second intervals) is a close cousin.

## 4. How Do You Do Tabata on a Rowing Machine? (20 Minutes, Advanced)


Advanced · 20 minutes


1. **Warm up:** 5 minutes easy, with two 20-second pickups
2. **Tabata 1:** 8 rounds of 20 seconds all-out (9 to 10 out of 10), then 10 seconds easy (4 minutes)
3. **Reset:** 2 minutes easy
4. **Tabata 2:** 8 more rounds (4 minutes)
5. **Cool down:** 5 minutes easy


Ten seconds of rest is barely any rest, so save this one until the first three feel comfortable. Keep the handle moving lightly during the 10-second breaks rather than stopping dead, or you'll lose a stroke or two getting back up to speed. On the Strong Series, Tabata Takeoff (9 to 27 minutes) is the guided version, and Quick Strike (2 to 7 minutes of sprints) makes a brutal finisher.

## 5. What's a Good 30-Minute Rowing Interval Workout?


Intermediate to advanced · 30 minutes


1. **Warm up:** 5 minutes easy
2. **Intervals:** 4 rounds of 4 minutes hard (7 to 8 out of 10), with 2 minutes easy between them
3. **Cool down:** 3 minutes easy


This is a rowing take on the 4x4 from a[2007 Norwegian study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17414804/) . Runners held 90 to 95% of their max heart rate for four minutes at a time and improved their VO2max (a key measure of aerobic fitness) more than groups doing moderate, steady training. The trick is pacing: row the first interval as if you had to do a fifth. On the Strong Series, Peak Pursuit (20 to 50 minutes of high-intensity intervals) is the closest match.

## How Often Should You Do HIIT Rowing?


Two to three times a week, with easier days in between. The[American Council on Exercise](https://www.acefitness.org/continuing-education/certified/april-2020/7494/ask-ace-high-intensity-interval-training/) (ACE) recommends 48 to 72 hours of recovery between HIIT sessions. If you do three or four a week, don't schedule more than two in a row.


More isn't automatically better. In research ACE summarizes, fitness gains were about the same whether people did HIIT two, three or four times a week. Longer sessions and more weekly HIIT time predicted more people dropping out. So start with two sessions a week you can keep up, and add a third once they feel routine.


Some people do work up to four. Sharon Maybrier did:


"From 0 exercise to 4 times a week interval workouts."


**Sharon Maybrier** , Aviron owner · Verified Buyer


A simple week to start with:


- **Monday:** Workout 1 or 3
- **Tuesday:** an easy 20-minute row, or a scenic one
- **Thursday:** Workout 2 or 5
- **Saturday:** a game or race at whatever pace feels fun

## What Are the Most Common HIIT Rowing Mistakes?


- **Pulling with your arms first.** The drive goes legs, then body, then arms. Lead with your arms and your biceps will be cooked by round two. Our[rowing form guide](https://www.avironactive.com/blog/correct-rowing-machine-form-fix-4-common-mistakes/) covers the fix.
- **Maxing out the resistance.** Heavier doesn't make it HIIT. Pick a level where you can hold good form for the whole interval, then make the work harder by pushing harder.
- **Skipping the warm-up.** Your first hard stroke of the session shouldn't also be your first stroke of the day.
- **Grinding through broken form.** When your back starts rounding, end the round early. One extra rep isn't worth a sore back.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Can you do HIIT on a rowing machine?


Yes, and it's one of the best machines for it. Alternate hard efforts of 20 seconds to 4 minutes with easy rowing. A rower is low impact, works most of your major muscle groups, and lets you change intensity within a few strokes.


### How long should a HIIT rowing workout be?


10 to 30 minutes, including warm-up and cool-down. The hard work itself usually adds up to 2 to 16 minutes. If you can keep going well past 30 minutes, you probably aren't working hard enough in the hard intervals.


### Is HIIT rowing good for beginners?


Yes, once you know the stroke. Spend a session or two rowing easy and focusing on technique, then start with Workout 1. Our guide to[your first month of rowing](https://www.avironactive.com/blog/rowing-for-beginners-first-month/) walks through it. If you have a heart condition or haven't exercised in a while, check with your doctor before doing high-intensity work.


### Is HIIT rowing better than steady rowing for weight loss?


For fat loss it's about equal, but HIIT takes less time. A[2017 meta-analysis of 13 trials](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28401638/) found that HIIT and moderate continuous training reduced body fat by similar amounts, with HIIT taking about 40% less time. Mixing both works well. More in[Is Rowing Good for Weight Loss?](https://www.avironactive.com/blog/is-rowing-good-for-weight-loss/)


### What resistance should I use for HIIT rowing?


A moderate level you can hold with good form for the full interval. Make the hard intervals harder by driving harder with your legs, not by cranking the resistance. Save the higher levels for slower, strength-focused pieces.
